               <ns0:p n="6">6 If a man abide not in me <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 3.10. and 7.19.</ns0:note>, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Our Lord yet pursueth the <ns0:hi>Metaphor</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Vine,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Branches,</ns0:hi> and the Husbandman: Look (saith he), as it is with a <ns0:hi>Vine,</ns0:hi> when the time of pruning the Vine cometh, the Vine-dresser cutteth off the fruitless luxuriant branches, and throweth them by, which being done, their greenness pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sently abateth, and they wither,</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">and after a time, some come and gather them up, and cast them into some fire, where they are burned: so it will be with you; if you do not bring forth fruit, God will take from you his common influences, which have for a while made you to look speci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ously, and your Profession, or your Parts and Gifts will wi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther and decay, and in the day of Judgment the Angels, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 13 40, 41. shall gather you up, and God shall cast you i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>to Hell, where you shall perish as miserably, nay, infi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tely more miserably than if you were burned with <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note>, and men gather them,
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:362" />
and cast <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> into the fire, and they are burn<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed <ns0:hi>n.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Here our Lord expounds what he meaneth by that <ns0:hi>abi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding in him</ns0:hi> which he before mentioned by another phrase [<ns0:hi>and my words abide in you</ns0:hi>], my precepts and promises, so as you by faith embrace the promises, and by <ns0:hi>obedience</ns0:hi> live up to the precepts which I have given you: for without these, tho the words of Christ may come unto men in the preaching of the Gospel, their ears may receive the sound of them, yet the Word doth not dwell and abide in the soul: but if the Word abides in the souls of men and wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />men,</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">then they may in prayer ask of God what they will, keeping to the conditions and limitations elsewhere re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quired in holy Writ, according to God's Will, 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 5.14. believing, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 21.22. in the Name of Christ, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 14.13, 14. for the honour and glory of God (to which end all our actions must be directed), and they shall be granted to us.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 16.</ns0:note>, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you <ns0:hi>p</ns0:hi>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit <ns0:hi>q,</ns0:hi> so shall ye be my Disci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">And tho men must be Christ's Disci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples before they bring forth any fruit, yet their bringing forth much fruit is that which alone can evidence and make them appear to be the Disciples of Christ. And often in Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture <ns0:hi>being</ns0:hi> signifieth <ns0:hi>appearing,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 8.31. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 3.4.</ns0:note>.<ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Here are Two Arguments to press his Disciples <ns0:hi>abiding in him,</ns0:hi> that so they might bring forth much fruit. 1. Here<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in (saith our Saviour) is my Father <ns0:hi>glorified.</ns0:hi> The glorify<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of God is the great end of our lives, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.31. God is glorified by men and womens bringing forth much fruit, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 5.16. the <ns0:hi>fruit unto holinese,</ns0:hi> Rom. 6.22. fruit in the product of the Plant, from the natural moisture that is in it, nourished and augmented by the fatness of the Earth in which it stands, and by the warmth of the Sun drawn out to the producing of such effects, according to the nature of the Plant. According to the different nature of Plants they bring forth various fruits, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 7.16, 17, 18. Hence we read of the <ns0:hi>fruit of sin unto death,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>fruit of righteousness unto life.</ns0:hi> The first is every man's natural fruit, until he be ingrafted into Christ: being ingrafted into him, the soul having a new Nature given to it, being regene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rated and renewed by the Holy Ghost, it no longer bringeth forth fruit from its old Principle, and according to its old nature, but from its new Principle, and according to its new nature; as the cultivated Earth that is plowed and har<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rowed, doth not bring forth Weeds and ordinary Grass, ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to its nature, but bringeth forth fruit according to the Seed that is cast into it, yet not without the influence of Heaven, both with respect to the dew of it, and the warmth which it hath from the Sun; so the soul being regenerated, the fallow ground of it being plowed up, and the seed of righteousness being sown in it, it no more brings forth the weeds of lusts and corruptions, or onely ordinary acts of humane nature, but it brings forth fruits according to its new nature, and the new seed of the Word now sown in it, and dwelling in it. And look, as it tendeth to the honour of the Husbandman, when the ground by him plowed and manured, brings forth much fruit; so it tendeth to the honour and glory of God, when t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e souls renewed, manured, and influenced by him, bring forth much of the fruit of righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ousness and holiness.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you: continue ye in my love <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">What our Saviour before called an <ns0:hi>abiding in him,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>his words abiding in us,</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>bearing</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>bringing forth much fruit,</ns0:hi> he here calleth a <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ontinuing in his love,</ns0:hi> tho in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deed this phrase also may be interpreted by a continuance in the favour of God and Christ, in that state of love into which God hath put the souls of those who are his true Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples: But I had rather interpret it of that <ns0:hi>love</ns0:hi> wherewith they loved Christ, than that wherewith Christ loved them. So the former words are an Argument to perswade perseve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rance, or a continuance in those acts of holiness by which men alone can shew their true love to Jesus Christ, from Christs love to them which he there expresseth; <ns0:hi>As the Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther hath loved me, so I have loved you</ns0:hi>; where the particle <ns0:hi>as,</ns0:hi> is onely a note of <ns0:hi>comparison,</ns0:hi> but doth not denote an <ns0:hi>equality</ns0:hi>; onely signifieth <ns0:hi>truth</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>greatness</ns0:hi>; As truly and sincerely as the Father loveth me; Or I have loved you with a <ns0:hi>great love,</ns0:hi> bearing some proportion to the love wherewith <ns0:hi>my Father loveth me</ns0:hi>; the Fathers love to Christ is <ns0:hi>Eternal, Immutable, Constant,</ns0:hi> full, and perfect, <ns0:hi>Wise,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iust, free</ns0:hi> in all these respects; Christ loveth his people as the Father loveth him: this ought to ingage them again to love him, and so to walk, as they may continue in that state of favour into which his goodness hath advanced them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 14.21, 25.</ns0:note> If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Abiding in Christs love</ns0:hi> in this verse, may be interpreted as before, either <ns0:hi>actively</ns0:hi>; you shall continue your love to me according to what we had, <ns0:hi>Chap</ns0:hi> 14.15. Obedience to the commandments of Christ, being the onely way to shew and declare the truth of our love to Christ. Or else <ns0:hi>passively,</ns0:hi> you shall keep your selves in my favour, I will love you:</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Thus I abide in my Fathers love; I do not shew love to my Father by my words and expressions onely, nor by per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />formance of some ceremonial ritual services, which he hath required; but by fulfilling his whole Will and Counsel, by yeilding an <ns0:hi>Obedience</ns0:hi> to him in all things. I love you as my Father loveth me: and you must abide in my love, by the same ways and means that I abide in my Fathers love The Disciple is not above his Master, nor the Servant above his Lord.</ns0:note>, even as I have kept my Fathers commandments, and abide in his love <ns0:hi>n.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">The end of my pressing so much the duty of holiness upon you, under the notions of abiding in me, abiding in my love, in my words, bringing forth much fruit, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> is, that I might have a continual cause to rejoice in you. Joy is nothing else but the satisfaction of the reasonable Soul in its union with an object which it loved and desired. Christ willing and desiring the perfection of his Disciples, accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to the rational workings of human nature; is properly said to rejoice in the satisfaction of his will, in which sense joy and rejoicing, are often in Scripture attributed to God.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 16.24.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> your joy might be full <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Nor doth Christ press them to this, that he might rejoice in them, but also that <ns0:hi>their joy might be full:</ns0:hi> That <ns0:hi>Ioy</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Peace</ns0:hi> which attends and follows believing, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 15.13. Called the <ns0:hi>peace of God. Colos.</ns0:hi> 3.15. <ns0:hi>A peace which passeth all understanding, Philip.</ns0:hi> 4.7. No man maketh Christ to <ns0:hi>rejoice over him,</ns0:hi> but he thereby also procureth unspeakable <ns0:hi>joy</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>peace to himself.</ns0:hi> As no man <ns0:hi>grieveth</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>Spirit,</ns0:hi> but also purchaseth grief and sadness to himself in the latter end.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Thes. 4.9. 1 Pet. 4 8. 1 John 3.23. and 4.21.</ns0:note> This is my commandment, That ye love one another, as I have loved you <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">This is that which our Lord called the new command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 13.34. (see the notes there.) He had before pressed the <ns0:hi>keeping of his words, continuing,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>abiding in his wo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ds, keeping his commandments, &c.</ns0:hi> Here he tells them what was his commandment: not his onely command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, but that which he laid a very great st<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ess upon; a commandment most necessary to be pressed, because so ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cessary to keep up and uphold his Church in the World; (love being the very ligament of that Society) and because there was a greater failure in obedience to this, than in some others, as may be learned from our Saviours correction of the Pharisees interpretation of that Law, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 5. This he presseth to an higher degree, as he had loved them; not that it is possible that our love to our Brethren, can rise up in any proportion to that love wherewith Christ hath loved us; but to mind us to eye him, to press forward toward this mark. <ns0:hi>As</ns0:hi> here again doth not signifie <ns0:hi>equality,</ns0:hi> but a <ns0:hi>comparison</ns0:hi>; as truly and sincerely as I have loved you, and pressing after the highest degree of love.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 5.7<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> Greater love hath no man then this, that a man lay down his life for his friends <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">The reason of this is, because <ns0:hi>Life</ns0:hi> is the greatest <ns0:hi>Earth<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly good</ns0:hi> to men under ordinary circumstances; <ns0:hi>Skin for skin and all a man hath, for his life.</ns0:hi> Now it is impossible that a man should shew a greater love to another, than by parting with the greatest good he is in possession of for his sake. Hence our Saviour proves, that he loved them with the greatest love, because he for their sake was about to part with, what in the common judgment of men is the greatest good. The greatness of the love of Christ to us, is from hence often commended to us in Scripture; and our mutual love to our Brethren is pressed upon this argument, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 5.2. 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 3.16. But how did Christ lay down his life for his friends? when the Scripture tells us, <ns0:hi>That the just died for the unjust,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Pet</ns0:hi> 3.18. and <ns0:hi>that while we were ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies, we were reconciled unto God by the Death of his Son, Rom.</ns0:hi> 5.10. <ns0:hi>Ans. Friends</ns0:hi> must not here be taken as a name of <ns0:hi>Relation,</ns0:hi> but onely as it signifieth the <ns0:hi>objects of love</ns0:hi>; per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons we have set our love upon, whither they mutually love us or no, as the World was the object of that love in God, which moved him to send his onely begotten Son, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 3.16. Tho they for whom Christ dyed, were enemies by their wicked works, yet by his death they were <ns0:hi>reconciled</ns0:hi>; but possibly the first answer is best, for by Christs Death they were onely meritoriously reconciled, and after this enemies to God, till they received the word of reconciliation, and believed in Christ.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:362" />14 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 14.15. See Matth. 12.50.</ns0:note> Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Our Lord presseth obedience to his commandments as a means, and indeed the onely means by which we can de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clare our love to Christ, and also useth a new argument to press their obedience, from his assuming them into the <ns0:hi>state</ns0:hi> and dignity of his friends.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 Henceforth I call you not servants, for the servant knoweth not what his lord doth <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">By his saying, I call you not <ns0:hi>servants,</ns0:hi> he doth not dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />charge them of that duty and service which they owed to him; for in pressing them to obey his commandments, he declareth that duty they owed to him; he onely sheweth that they were no ordinary servants, but taken into a state of dignity, favour, and familiarity, beyond that of servants, and that he had not treated them like servants, but like intimate familiar friends.</ns0:note>: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father, I have made known unto you <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">For look as ordinary masters in the World, communicate their counsels, and whole heart to their friends, especially in things which are of any concern, or may be of any advantage for them to know and under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand: whereas they keep themselves at distance from ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vants, and they onely know so much of their minds as is by them to be done in their masters service: so he had not onely revealed to them their duty, what was to be by them done in his service, but had been more free, giving to them to know the <ns0:hi>mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven</ns0:hi>; as he told them, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 13.11. as well telling them his Fathers coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sels on the behalf of them, and whatsoever he might com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />municate to them, as his Fathers Will; what he would have them to do in obedience to his commandments.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Jo. 4.10, 19.</ns0:note> Ye have not chosen me <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">You have not chosen me to be your Lord, Master, Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour,</ns0:note>, but I have cho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sen you, and <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Matth. 28.19. Mark 16.15. Colos. 1.6.</ns0:note> ordained you, that you should go and bring forth fruit <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">for this end, to bring forth fruit amongst the Gentiles, turning many to Righteousness, and that they might bring forth the fruit of holiness, in obedience to the Gospel of Christ.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> your fruit should remain <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Yea, not onely to bring forth fruit, but that they might persevere in bringing forth fruit;</ns0:note>: that <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Ver. 7.</ns0:note> whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my Name, he may give it you <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">and that thus doing, they might have a freedom of access to the Throne of Grace, and obtain whatsoever they should ask of the Father, in the Name, for the merits, and through the Mediation of the Lord Jesus Christ. See the notes on <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 14.13, 14.</ns0:note>.<ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">but I have chosen and <ns0:hi>ordained you</ns0:hi>: so we have it in our translation: but the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> is, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, I have set you, or placed you in a station What chusing Christ here speaks of, is doubted amongst various Divines. Some think that our Saviour here speaks of his choice of them to the Apostleship, as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 6.13. <ns0:hi>Chap</ns0:hi> 6. <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 70. those who thus understand it, understand it by <ns0:hi>going,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>bringing forth fruit</ns0:hi>; the Apostles going out, <ns0:hi>Preaching,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Baptizing</ns0:hi> all <ns0:hi>Nations,</ns0:hi> bringing forth fruit amongst the Gentiles. But others un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstand it, of <ns0:hi>election to eternal Life,</ns0:hi> and the means ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cessary to it; for our Saviour brings this as an argument of his greatest love: <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> was in the first sense chosen, yet not beloved with any such love; and this seemeth to be favoured by <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 13.18. <ns0:hi>I speak not of you all, I know whom I have chosen</ns0:hi>: and certain it is, <ns0:hi>Augustine,</ns0:hi> and others of the An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cients from hence proved the freedom of <ns0:hi>Election,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>spe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cial Grace.</ns0:hi> Both senses may be united; for the <ns0:hi>Eleven</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> (to whom Christ was now speaking) were chosen in both senses; they were chosen</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 These things I command you, that ye love one another <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">This is but the repetition of the same precept we before had, unless we will understand it as a more special charge upon them, considered as Ministers of the Gospel; the mu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tual love of Ministers, being highly necessary for the good and peace of the Church of God, over which God hath set them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Joh. 3.13.</ns0:note> If the world hate you <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">In this latter part of this <ns0:hi>Chapter,</ns0:hi> our Lord cometh to comfort those who were his true Disciples, against that third trouble, from the prospect they had of that hatred which the World would pour out, and execute upon them, assoon as he should be withdrawn from them. <ns0:hi>Hatred</ns0:hi> is rooted, and originated in the heart, and is properly a dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pleasure that the mind taketh at a person, which fermenting, and boiling in the mind, breeds an abhorrence of that per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son, anger, and malice, and a desire to do him mischief, and root him out, and then breaks out at the lips, by lying, slan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ders, calumnies, cursings, wishing of evil, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> and is exe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cuted by the hands, doing to such persons all the harm and mischief, within the power of him that hateth: All this is to be understood under the general term <ns0:hi>Hate.</ns0:hi> By the World here, must be meant <ns0:hi>wicked men,</ns0:hi> in opposition to good men, who are often in Scripture called the World, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause they are of the earth earthly; they relish and savour nothing but worldly things, and pursue nothing but worldly designs. Against this our Saviour comforts them, first by telling them, That this part of the World hated him before it hated them, which must needs be so, because they ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted them as his Disciples, and for that very reason.</ns0:note>, ye know that it hated me before <ns0:hi>it hated</ns0:hi> you <ns0:hi>l.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 John 4.5.</ns0:note> If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Chap. 17.14.</ns0:note> because ye are not of the world <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Men and Women may be in the World, yet not of the <ns0:hi>World. Of the World,</ns0:hi> here signifies carnal men, such as are like to the men of the World in their studies, designs, coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sels, affections; as <ns0:hi>of the Devil,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>of God</ns0:hi> signifies, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 8.44, 47. If you had affections, lusts, and dispositions like them, and drave no other designs than they drive, you might expect that as it is of the nature of all men to love such as are like to them in manners and studies; so they would love you, take a delight in you, be kind to you, and do you all offices of love:</ns0:note>, but I have chosen you out of the world <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">but because you are not of such tempers, dispositions and inclinations, but that I having chosen you out of the World, have given you new hearts, new frames and dispositions, quite contrary to theirs; therefore the World disliking you, and seeing that your principles are quite opposite to theirs, abhor, and hate you, and will be ready to do you all that evil and mischief<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> which is the product of a rooted hatred and malice in the heart: This is a second argument by which our Lord comforts them. It is drawn from the cause and root of that hatred, which they would meet with: it was not for their faults or sins, but because they were the objects of Christs love, which being also shed abroad in their hearts by the holy Ghost, produced again in them holy affections and dispositions, making them wholly unlike to men in the World.</ns0:note>, therefore the world hateth you <ns0:hi>o.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Remember the word that I said unto you <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The word that I said unto you, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 13.16. to press you to humility, and a mutual serving of one another in love, and which I spake to you, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.24. when I first sent you out, and I spake it then to you upon the very same ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />count, that I now speak it.</ns0:note>, The servant is not greater then the lord: If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Ezek. 3.7.</ns0:note>
                  <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> if they have kept my saying, they will keep yours also <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">You that are my servants, cannot look to fare better with the World, than I that am your Master, you know they have hated me, you must ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pect they should persecute you: if there be any of them whose hearts God shall incline to keep my sayings, they will also keep your words, which are but my sayings explained to them, and further pressed upon them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matt. 24.9. Chap. 16.3.</ns0:note> all these things will they do unto you for my Names sake <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>For my Names sake,</ns0:hi> here signifies no more than for <ns0:hi>my sake,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.22. for your Preaching, owning, and professing me and my Gospel:</ns0:note>, because they know not him that sent me <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">and this they would not do, if they had any true knowledge of faith in, or love for him that sent me: for <ns0:hi>knowing</ns0:hi> (as hath been often said) in holy Writ, and particularly in this Gospel, signifieth not the bare comprehension of the object by our understanding, but such a comprehension of it, as is operative and efficacious, to the bringing forth of all such effects, as are proper to such a knowledge and comprehension. So as this text containeth two arguments more, to arm them against the hatred of the World: The first, from the honourableness of the cause, for Christs Names sake. The second from the ignorance and blindness of the persons.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9 41.</ns0:note> If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">The<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> had not had this particular sin, of not knowing him that sent me: Or they had not had such degrees of sin, as they now have; or they had had more to say in excuse, or for a cover for their sin. Ignorance of the Will of God will not excuse sinners wholly, but it will excuse them in part; and this last seemeth to be the sense of the words by the latter part of the Verse, because it is opposed to an ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving no cloak nor excuse for their sin. If Christ had not come in his Incarnation, in his Preaching the Gospel, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> they could not have been guilty of that hatred, and malice which they shewed against him, which was their greatest guilt; and the<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> would have had this to say, Lord! we know not what Christ was, as <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 25.44. but now saith our Saviour, they have no cloak, no colour, no pretence, I am come, I have revealed my Fathers mind and will to them, yet they will not receive me: no, tho I have done those works before them, which no man ever did, nor could do but by a Divine Power.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Rom. 1.20.</ns0:note> but now they have no <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, Excuse.</ns0:note> cloak for their sin <ns0:hi>u.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:363" />23 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Joh. 2 23.</ns0:note> He that hateth me, hateth my Father also <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">This agreeth with what we had, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 5.23. It is a common error of the World, that many in it would pretend to love God, while yet they are manifest haters of Christ and his Gospel: Now saith our Saviour, This is impossible; who<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />soever hateth him who is sent, hateth also him that sent him. God the Father, and Christ are one, and no man can hate Christ, or be an enemy to Christ, but he must be an enemy to his Father: and as this is an aggravation of their sin, so it is a great argument of consolation to the Disciples of Christ, that those who should be their enemies, were such as were in reality Gods enemies.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 If I had not done among them the works which none other man did, they had not had sin <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Our Saviour often appealeth to his works, both to own his Mission from God, and also to prove the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> in excusa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble, in their not receiving and imbracing him: for which latter purpose he mentions them here, and saith, that he had done such works as no man did, and by his <ns0:hi>own Power</ns0:hi> and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Christ did some works, as we do not read, that eve<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> man did; such as the multiplying of the loaves, the giving sight to those that were born blind, the healing of so many desperate diseases: And for such as he did, which God had also given men a power to do, he did them in a quite different manner from that in which men did them. <ns0:hi>Elisha</ns0:hi> raised the <ns0:hi>Shunamites</ns0:hi> child to life, but it was by Prayer<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> cured the lame man, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 3.6. but it was <ns0:hi>in the Name of Iesus Christ of Nazareth.</ns0:hi> We read indeed of Christs praying at the raising of <ns0:hi>Lazarus</ns0:hi>; but his ordinary way, was by his word of command, which was a quite dif<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ferent way than that used by those men, by whom miracles had been wrought Besides, it is manifest, that the gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rality of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> did not look upon Christ as one sent from God, tho many of them did; and admit that there had been nothing in the miracles wrought by Christ, more than <ns0:hi>Elijah,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Elisha,</ns0:hi> or the Prophets had done; yet it had been suffi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cient for to have convinced them, that he acted by a Divine Power, and must be sent and Authoriz'd by and from God to do what he did. Now saith our Saviour, if I had not done before their faces, such works as no man could do but by a Power derived from God, and some such as God never authorized men to do; their sin had been nothing to what now it is:</ns0:note>: but now have they both seen, and hated both me and my Father <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">but now they have understood, that I am sent from my Father; and knowing this, yet going on in their most malicious designs against me, they both declare an ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tred and malice against my Father who sent me, and me as sent by him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 But <ns0:hi>this cometh to pass,</ns0:hi> that the word might be fulfilled that is written in their law <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">The particle [<ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi>] here again denoteth not the final cause, but onely the <ns0:hi>consequent</ns0:hi>; and the <ns0:hi>Law</ns0:hi> here signifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth not strictly the <ns0:hi>Law of Moses,</ns0:hi> but the whole Scripture, (in which sense we have once and again met with the term) saith our Saviour, This is no more than was Prophecied of me, by the Prophet <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>; or no more than was fulfill<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed in me, being first done to <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> as my Type, which also hath the force of another <ns0:hi>Argument</ns0:hi> to uphold, and in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />courage his Disciples under their sufferings; that they were but the fulfilling of Prophecies, no more than was foretold in holy Writ.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 35.19. and 69.4.</ns0:note>, They hated me without a cause.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 24 49.</ns0:note> But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Concerning the Holy Ghost as a <ns0:hi>Comforter,</ns0:hi> we have spoken <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>argely, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 14.16, 26. as also his mission from the Father and the Son, and in what sense he is called the Spirit of truth: <ns0:hi>see the notes on those Verse.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">What pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceeding from the Father, is here meant, is questioned a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst Divines: some understand it onely of his coming out from the Father, and being poured out upon the Disciples in the days of Pentecost: Others understand it of the holy Spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rits <ns0:hi>Eternal proceeding.</ns0:hi> Those that Interpret it of the first, urge the use of the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word, here used to signifie Gods manifestation of himself, by some external sign, (as they say the <ns0:hi>Septuagint</ns0:hi> useth the same word.) They also urge the same use of a parallel word, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 8.42. and 16.28. But the generality of the best Interpreters think, it is best under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood of the <ns0:hi>Eternal procession of the holy Spirit.</ns0:hi> Because Christ here distinguisheth the Spirits proceeding from the Father, from <ns0:hi>his sending.</ns0:hi> 2. Having himself promised to send the Spirit, he seemeth further to describe him, as <ns0:hi>pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceeding from the Father.</ns0:hi> 3. The word here used, is not any where used in the New Testament to signifie a Temporal mission, some will say, but <ns0:hi>doth not the Spirit proceed from the Son? Ans.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Greek Church</ns0:hi> in latter ages hath denied this, and this is the principal text they rest on; but those Churches that are more Orthodox have constantly affirmed it. 1. Because he here saith he would send it. 2. Because he is often called the Spirit of Christ, <ns0:hi>Rom</ns0:hi> 8.9. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 4.6.3. Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause otherwise there were no personal relation between <ns0:hi>Christ and the Spirit.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour here having first said he would send him, here onely nameth his <ns0:hi>proceeding from the Father</ns0:hi>; that they might not suspect his testimony, or think that he spake arrogantly.</ns0:note>, he shall testifie of me <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The Spirit he saith should testifie of him, both by those gifts with which he was to fill the Apostles, and to the hearts of Gods people.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 1.8, 22.</ns0:note> ye also shall bear witness, because <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Luke 1.2.</ns0:note> ye have been with me from the beginning <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">He adds also, <ns0:hi>They should testifie, &c.</ns0:hi> The Apostles and their Successors by the Preaching of the Gospel; but particularly the Apostles, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 10.39. 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.2, 3. being <ns0:hi>chosen witnesses, Acts</ns0:hi> 10.41. And they were <ns0:hi>competent wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nesses,</ns0:hi> because they had been with Christ from the begin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning of his publick Ministry. We shall find the Testimony of his <ns0:hi>Apostles,</ns0:hi> and of the <ns0:hi>Holy Ghost,</ns0:hi> both joined together, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 5.32.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
